notes: Read all six units, full tax-policy context, all seven candidates and the review. Resolved current filing rules as the existing IRS tax-code rules. Identified the allegedly best gradual approach as the transitional choice between those rules and a two-rate flat tax, removing the lobbyist-legions metaphor. Restored the condition that the value-added-tax or national-sales-tax restriction applies during fundamental federal-tax restructuring.

claims.claim_text: As a transition, taxpayers should be allowed to file under existing IRS tax-code rules or a two-rate flat tax with generous family deductions.
The transitional choice between existing IRS rules and a two-rate flat tax is characterized as taxpayers' best chance to overcome lobbying that previously blocked tax simplification.

During any fundamental restructuring of federal taxation, a value-added tax or national sales tax must be paired with simultaneous repeal of the Sixteenth Amendment to guard against excessive taxation.
